judge_output.rationale: The idea that partial Dyson spheres produce a waste-heat infrared excess separable from natural dust has been tested several times. Hephaistos II (2024MNRAS.531..695S) and Hephaistos I (2022MNRAS.512.2988S) did this with Gaia, 2MASS and WISE broadband photometry, and Carrigan (2009ApJ...698.2075C) fitted 100-600 K blackbodies to IRAS low-resolution spectra. None of the listed works uses low-resolution 0.75-5 um spectra such as SPHEREx, or tests whether the excess shape across 2-5 um is spectrally distinct from debris-disc dust. The card is therefore the same claim in a new archive with a spectral rather than photometric observable.

closest_prior.relation: Tested partial-Dyson-sphere IR excess against a blackbody-plus-photosphere model using Gaia DR3, 2MASS and WISE photometry over ~5 million sources, yielding seven M-dwarf candidates; it used broadband filters, not 0.75-5 um spectra.

Set upper limits on 100-1000 K partial Dyson spheres from Gaia DR2 and AllWISE colours, including ~2.7e5 stars within 100 pc; photometric colour cuts only, with no spectral-shape discrimination from dust.
Fitted 100-600 K blackbodies to IRAS LRS spectra (roughly 8-22 um) to search for partial or full Dyson spheres; it is spectral but at longer wavelengths and much shallower depth than SPHEREx.
Showed that most Hephaistos candidates' mid-IR excesses are likely background dust-obscured galaxy contamination, a confounder the card must handle, but it does not test the spectral-shape claim.

judge_output.what_would_make_it_open: A SPHEREx R~35-130 analysis would add a measurement of the 2-5 um excess spectral shape for G<12 stars within 100 pc, and a test of whether any smooth blackbody-like excess is separable from debris-disc dust features, which broadband WISE/2MASS photometry and longer-wavelength IRAS spectra could not resolve.

judge_output.rationale: The card measures the spectral shape of a smooth 2-5 um excess across the roughly 100 SPHEREx channels at R >= 35, and asks whether that shape separates partial-swarm-like waste heat from debris-disc dust. Project Hephaistos I and II (2022MNRAS.512.2988S, 2024MNRAS.531..695S), Contardo et al. (2024AJ....168..157C) and Blain (2024arXiv240911447B) all rest on broadband 2MASS/WISE photometry, which can show that an excess exists but cannot resolve its 2-5 um spectral shape. Carrigan (2009ApJ...698.2075C) did fit blackbody spectral shapes, but only to IRAS LRS spectra at about 8-23 um for bright sources, not the near-IR Wien side of the excess. No listed work measures this shape-based quantity, so the claim has not been tested.

closest_prior.relation: Fit 100-600 K blackbody shapes to IRAS LRS mid-IR spectra (~8-23 um) of bright sources; it did not measure the 2-5 um excess shape at SPHEREx depth.
Hephaistos II fit photosphere-plus-blackbody SEDs to Gaia/2MASS/WISE broadband photometry for ~5 million stars; it measured band excesses, not a resolved 2-5 um spectral shape.
Hephaistos I set upper limits from Gaia-AllWISE colour cuts; it counted objects in colour regions and did not measure spectral shape.
Data-driven W1/W2 excess search in about 4.9 million FGK stars aimed at extreme debris discs; it measured two-band excess amplitude only, not shape discrimination from dust.
